dimensions.assessment: Affects individual taxpayers whose tax returns are altered or filed fraudulently by preparers without the taxpayer's knowledge, as well as the IRS.
dimensions.evidence: limits the amount of time the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) has to assess taxes related to fraudulent or false federal tax returns where there is no intent by the taxpayer to evade taxes

dimensions.assessment: Alters the tax assessment window for affected taxpayers, shielding them from indefinite assessment periods under the fraud exception when they lacked intent to evade taxes.
dimensions.evidence: Section 6501(c)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting 'by the taxpayer' after 'intent'.

dimensions.assessment: Potential localized reduction in tax collections or penalties for affected taxpayers, though no aggregate fiscal estimates are provided.
Makes a targeted statutory amendment to section 6501(c)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code and a technical amendment regarding disaster deadlines.
dimensions.evidence: Section 6501(c)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting 'by the taxpayer' after 'intent'.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent amendment to the Internal Revenue Code applicable to assessments made or proceedings begun after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendment made by this section shall apply to assessments made or proceedings begun after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: The exact number of taxpayers affected annually by preparer fraud extensions.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill clarifies the statute of limitations exception for false or fraudulent tax returns, restricting the IRS's ability to assess taxes beyond the standard three-year period in cases of preparer fraud where the taxpayer lacked intent to evade taxes.
